stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Highway engineers in one state compared cracking on roads surfaced with a new rubber-modified asphalt against roads surfaced with conventional asphalt. After eight years, the rubber-modified roads showed about 40 percent less cracking. However, because of how construction contracts were awarded, most of the rubber-modified roads were in the state's southern counties. Those counties go through far fewer freeze-thaw cycles each winter than the northern counties, and freeze-thaw cycles are a major cause of pavement cracking. The lower cracking rate on the rubber-modified roads therefore ______
choices: may reflect the milder southern climate rather than any advantage of the new asphalt.
shows that the new asphalt is no more durable than the conventional asphalt is.
proves that the new asphalt would resist cracking equally well in any region.
indicates that freeze-thaw cycles have little effect on how pavement cracks.
explanation: The flaw is a confound: the new asphalt was mostly laid where winters are mild, and mild winters by themselves mean less cracking. So you can't tell whether the asphalt or the climate caused the difference. Choice A says the result may come from the climate, and that's as far as the evidence goes.

B.why: You treated the confound as proof of the opposite result. The climate difference only makes the comparison uncertain. It doesn't show that the new asphalt performs no better.

C.why: You took a result from mostly mild-winter roads and applied it to every region. The passage gives you no data on harsh climates, and the confound means even the mild-climate result is unclear.

D.why: The passage says freeze-thaw cycles are a major cause of cracking. This choice reverses that.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Some musicologists argue that nineteenth-century violinists played slow movements much faster than violinists do today. As evidence, they point to wax-cylinder recordings made around 1900 by elderly players who trained in the 1850s. Historian Ruth Okonjo urges caution, however. A typical cylinder could hold only about two to four minutes of sound, so performers often had to finish a movement within that limit or cut it short. Given this constraint, the brisk tempos on the cylinders ______

might not accurately reflect the tempos these players chose in live concerts.
demonstrate that recording length had no influence on how the players performed.
reveal which slow movements were most popular with audiences of the 1850s.
explanation: The complication is the time limit of the medium. Players may have sped up to fit the cylinder, so the recorded tempos may not match how they really played. Choice B says only that the recordings might be misleading, and that's what Okonjo's point supports.

A.why: You swung to a firm conclusion in the other direction. The time limit makes the recordings unreliable, but it doesn't show that these players preferred slower tempos.

C.why: Okonjo's whole point is that the time limit may have shaped the performances. This choice says the opposite.

D.why: Audience preferences never come up. The passage is about whether the recordings show real performance tempos, not which pieces were popular.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In 2019, managers stocked Lake Marren with yellow perch, a fish that feeds on zooplankton. By the following summer, the lake's zooplankton density had fallen by more than half, and some ecologists attributed the drop to the perch. Because of this, the decline in zooplankton ______

proves that stocking perch will reduce zooplankton in any lake where it occurs.
can't be confidently attributed to the perch, since the heat may also have played a role.
suggests that water temperature has little effect on zooplankton populations.

A.why: You treated a possible cause as the proven cause. The heat is raised only as an alternative explanation, so it makes the perch explanation uncertain without ruling it out.

B.why: You stretched one confounded result from one lake to every lake. The study can't even establish what happened in Lake Marren.

D.why: The passage says prolonged heat can cut zooplankton numbers. This choice denies the mechanism the text describes.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

reveals that most residents in the region had studied at the university.
may understate how often residents use the ending in ordinary conversation.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Records from a regional network of rain gauges show that measured annual rainfall fell by nearly 8 percent between 1970 and 2010, and some climatologists have cited the decline as evidence of a drying trend. During those same decades, however, roughly half of the network's gauges were moved from open ground to the rooftops of nearby buildings, where stronger winds blow some raindrops past a gauge's opening before they can be caught. The recorded decline in rainfall therefore ______
choices: may partly reflect where the gauges were placed rather than how much rain actually fell.
shows that rooftop gauges caught more rain each year than gauges on open ground did.
proves that actual rainfall in the region rose steadily between 1970 and 2010.
confirms that the region's climate grew steadily drier between 1970 and 2010.
explanation: The flaw is that the gauges were moved to rooftops, where wind makes them catch less rain. A drop in measured rainfall could therefore come from the move rather than from any real change in rain. That makes the link between the records and a drying trend uncertain. It doesn't settle the question either way, so the cautious claim is the only one the passage supports.

B.why: You reversed the effect of the move. The passage says wind blows raindrops past rooftop gauges, so they would catch less rain than ground gauges, not more.

C.why: You saw that the evidence for a decline was weakened and decided the opposite must be true. The complication only removes certainty. Nothing in the passage shows that real rainfall increased.

D.why: You accepted the climatologists' original claim and skipped the 'however.' The gauge move is exactly what makes a firm conclusion about drying impossible.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Hydrologists reconstructing the flood history of a desert canyon have measured the high-water marks that floods leave on its walls, which are lines of silt and debris. The highest marks all date from the last forty years, which has led some researchers to argue that floods in the canyon have grown more severe. But the canyon's soft sandstone wears away quickly, and marks more than a few decades old are often eroded beyond recognition. The pattern in the high-water marks therefore ______
choices: might not indicate a real increase in flood severity, since older marks may have vanished.
indicates that floods before 1980 were more severe than any of the recent floods.
suggests that recent floods have sped the erosion of the canyon's sandstone walls.
demonstrates that floods in the canyon have grown more severe in recent decades.
explanation: The flaw is erosion: old high-water marks tend to disappear. If the oldest marks are missing, the record would make recent floods look like the biggest even if they weren't. So the pattern might not reflect a real change. The passage takes away the certainty without proving anything about the older floods.

B.why: You turned 'the older marks may be gone' into 'the older floods were bigger.' Missing evidence can't tell you how high those floods reached, so a firm claim in this direction is no better supported than the original one.

C.why: You latched onto erosion as the topic. The passage presents erosion as the reason the flood record may be incomplete, not as something the floods cause, and it says nothing about recent floods speeding it up.

D.why: You completed the view of 'some researchers' and ignored the 'But' that undercuts it. The erosion problem means the marks can't establish that floods have worsened.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In a three-year trial in Iowa, agronomists found that cornfields planted with a winter cover of crimson clover produced 11 percent more grain the following summer than fields left bare over winter. Every farm that planted clover, however, also stopped plowing its fields in the same year. The researchers had no clover fields that were still plowed and no bare fields that had stopped plowing. The higher yields in the clover fields therefore ______
choices: may not be attributable to the clover itself, since plowing changed at the same time.
resulted entirely from the decision to stop plowing rather than from the clover.
show that clover lowers corn yields on farms that continue to plow their fields.
suggest that the bare fields had poorer soil than the clover fields to begin with.

C.why: The passage says there were no plowed clover fields, so the trial says nothing about how clover performs where plowing continues. You invented a result for a condition nobody tested.

D.why: You added an extra step. Starting soil quality is never mentioned, and the confound the passage actually names is plowing. Nothing establishes that the bare fields had poorer soil.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: After painting protected bike lanes on five downtown streets, city officials reported that bicycle crashes on those streets fell by 30 percent over the following year. was caused by the bridge closure and would have occurred even without the new lanes.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In a large dietary study, adults who recorded high fiber intake in weekly food diaries tended to have lower blood cholesterol than those who recorded low intake. shows that dietary fiber has no real effect on the level of blood cholesterol.
proves that the participants with low cholesterol ate the least fiber of anyone.
confirms that eating more fiber lowers blood cholesterol in most healthy adults.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

show that the vaccine's protection fades well before six months have passed.
prove that catching the virus, not the vaccine, produced most of the antibodies.

stimulus: Many ecologists credit sea otters with protecting kelp forests, because otters eat the sea urchins that graze on kelp. the heatwave, not the otters, caused the decline in urchins.
the decline cannot be credited to otters with full confidence.
urchin numbers on the reef fell over the period surveyed.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

the island was once more than three times its present length.

fewer flooded streets were reported after the pavement went in.
